system.summary: Figures 1-53 for letters (two or three homophones, alphabetical), doubles and a null, 54-123 an alphabetical syllabary of fourteen consonants by five vowels, word-signs in letters and a few higher numbers.
system.doubled_letters: special sign (1 = ée, 2 = ll, square = ss)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's f. 321 key (same design, shifted by eight) used to read f. 333; f. 143 (1583) is another key, not read
system.notes: h has three homophones despite being a consonant; about a dozen letter-written word-signs and three numbers (180, 215?, 900) glossed or open.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's reconstructed f. 321 key (sibling); no plaintext of ff. 233, 239, 288v; G. Lasry solved it independently in 2024, unpublished (private communication, 25 Sept 2026)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: solve.py (structured annealer, 5-gram French LM, clear text as context)

solution.what: Gallica IIIF fetched with a browser User-Agent.
Frequencies of the upper figures mod 5 show blocks of five: an alphabetical syllabary.
Catherine de Médicis letters under random keys of the same shape; 64-start model 47-90 %, corrected 54-start model 96.6 %.
Structured annealer with the clear French as context recovers the key; syllabary start corrected from 64 to 54 by the reading.
Three letters read in substance; word-signs partly glossed.
f. 333 read with Tomokiyo's f. 321 key; whole volume swept, f. 366 found.
Free annealer on f. 333 alone fails (below unicity); matched control of the same size fails likewise.
Design-constrained annealer re-derives the f. 333 key blind, 93 % of letter tokens; matched alphabetical control 90 %.
f. 366 (24 tokens) tried with both keys; two of three lines do not read.
Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): Lasry wrote that he had independently solved it in 2024 but never published it; kept in the ciphertext-only list with that note.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 470 tokens, 103 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.066 per letter; random keys -4.259 (z 15.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.698 (mean -2.734, z 17.4); annealer on the real text -2.564. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.066; polyphony 0.0; 16 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.564

outcome.method_basis: A syllabary residue test and a structured annealer with the letters' clear French as language-model context rebuilt the ff. 233/239/288v key, confirmed on matched controls; Tomokiyo's sibling f. 321 key (on cryptiana before the attempt) has different offsets and was used only for f. 333.
outcome.notes: ff. 233, 239, 288v read in substance; f. 333 read with the sibling key; f. 366 left open; f. 143 (1583) another key, not read.

credits.note: solved it independently in 2024, unpublished (private communication, 25 Sept 2026)
